newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower except for gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower except for gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended slightly lower Monday, but COMEX gold managed to end higher, helped by news of an end to Belgian central bank gold sales.
But the U.S. Columbus Day holiday which shut banks and the federal government limited activity, traders said.

"We continue to feel gold prices are around the bottom of a trading range and that a sustained price advance is likely to occur if our assumptions of stronger physical demand and limited supply pressure from central banks and producers are realized," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
COMEX December gold ended up $0.40 at $383.80 an ounce after trading from $382.70 to $384.10.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted at $381.50/382.00 versus the London afternoon fix of $380.90 and the New York close Friday around $381.25.
Belgian National Bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said Monday there would be no more Belgian central bank gold sales, after sales of about 700 tonnes in recent years.
Last week rumors of further Belgian central bank gold sales circulated in precious metals markets.

Verplaetse said G-10 central bankers had an agreement not to destabilize the gold market, but said it was possible to sell one or two tonnes a day (2204-4408 troy ounces a day) without without upsetting the market. G-10 consists of the U.S., Germany, Japan, Canada, the U.K, France, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden.
The gold market may also benefit from higher seasonal Indian demand in coming weeks with two major Hinud festivals due against a background of another good monsoon and good harvest, analysts said.
India is the world's largest consumer of gold and demand is expected to rise about five to seven percent to around 450 tonnes in 1996.
COMEX December silver ended down 2.3 cents at $5.035 after trading from $5.06 to $5.01.
COMEX silver stocks, excluding Wilmington Trust silver stocks, fell a further 268,282 ounces Friday to 130,744,022 ounces, setting a fresh ten year low.

"Market participants continue to follow falling Comex reported and registered stocks closely, trying to determine the extent to which this represents fabricators and long term investors moving physical metal out of New York and the extent to which it may represent dealers playing with speculative sentiment," Kempf said.
Despite silver's weaker close Monday, silver was the leader in the recovery in the precious metals complex last week, as it was during the previous month-long decline, analysts said.
As a result the spot gold/silver ratio has fallen to around 76 at the close Monday, from 79 less than four weeks ago.
"This ratio is near the lower end of the range that has held for several years," Prudential Securities analyst Donald Selkin said.
NYMEX January platinum ended off $0.20 at $389.50 and NYMEX December palladium closed down $1.25 at $117.75.
